dimensions.assessment: Affects individual and corporate taxpayers who file tax returns or send correspondence in paper format to the IRS.
dimensions.evidence: This bill requires the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) to use barcodes, barcode scanning technology, and optical character recognition (or similar) technology to digitize certain federal tax return information and correspondence

dimensions.assessment: Changes technical formatting requirements for electronically prepared tax returns printed on paper and alters internal IRS document processing methods.
dimensions.evidence: Specifically, the bill requires a scannable barcode on electronically-prepared federal tax returns that are printed and filed in paper format with the IRS.

dimensions.assessment: Directs technology adoption by the IRS, but does not state specific implementation costs or federal spending levels.
Mandates specific technological processes for IRS document intake and transcription unless reporting exceptions are met.
dimensions.evidence: the Internal Revenue Service shall use optical character recognition technology (or any functionally similar technology) to transcribe such return or correspondence.

dimensions.assessment: Imposes permanent digitization requirements phased in across different return types starting after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: This section shall apply to--(1) any individual income tax return... received on or after January 1 of the first calendar year beginning more than 180 days after the date of enactment

missing_information: Cost estimates for purchasing or implementing barcode scanning and optical character recognition systems at the IRS.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires the IRS to digitize paper-filed tax returns and correspondence using scannable barcodes and optical character recognition technology, subject to exceptions.
